headline: Government Launches Task Force To Resolve 13 Severe Human Rights Cases
seoTitle: Indonesia Forms Task Force for Human Rights Cases
metaDescription: The Indonesian government established a cross-institutional working group to address procedural obstacles in 13 severe human rights violation cases.
aiSummaryBullets: A new cross-institutional working group has been established to resolve 13 long-standing cases of alleged severe human rights violations.
The initiative aims to address specific procedural hurdles that have hindered the legal progress of these historical matters.
Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra confirmed that the administration will not form a special team specifically focused on wiretapping allegations.
aiContextParagraph: The Indonesian government has initiated a cross-institutional working group, known as a Pokja, to expedite the resolution of 13 identified cases involving alleged severe human rights violations. This task force, led by Otto Hasibuan, is tasked with identifying and resolving systemic and procedural bottlenecks that have prevented these cases from reaching a final legal conclusion. Coordinating Minister for Law, Human Rights, Immigration, and Correctional Affairs Yusril Ihza Mahendra confirmed the formation of this body following high-level ministerial coordination meetings. Simultaneously, the government clarified its current administrative stance regarding other security-related concerns. Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra explicitly stated that there are currently no plans for the administration to establish a special team to address separate inquiries regarding wiretapping cases. This development represents a formal attempt by the current government to address long-pending human rights claims through dedicated institutional collaboration.
